prompt: a bioluminescent alien jungle, giant mushrooms and ferns, mist (features.md ART-06)

inquiry.setting: Fictional planet. Read as a dense, wet, lowland tropical forest: a few emergent giants above a closed canopy, a mid canopy of fast pioneers and palms, and a shaded understorey with tree ferns.
inquiry.method: structural analogue: the planet does not exist, so real species were chosen whose FORMS fit the described biome. They are Neotropical lowland rainforest species, one or two per forest layer. Their botanical structure is kept; only colour and glow are changed, through material parameters.
inquiry.not_covered: Giant mushrooms are not trees and are out of scope for this skill (make them with the blender-game-asset skill).

sources.UTP: Useful Tropical Plants Database, tropical.theferns.info (Ken Fern), species page, read 2026-11-12. Each fact below names the reference that page cites for it.
sources.WP: Wikipedia species article, read 2026-11-12. Used only for a sentence that carries a citation, which is named; uncited sentences are marked low confidence.

rules.range: When a source gives a range, the midpoint is used and the range is kept in 'range'.
rules.upper: A value marked basis 'upper' is the largest size the source documents, chosen on purpose (stated in 'why').
rules.qualitative: A clear-bole fraction is never measured in these sources. It is set only from a stated habit, by the fixed table in references/botanical-data.md (high-branching 0.6, short bole 0.15), and marked 'derived'. Otherwise it is left out.

height_m.why: the brief asks for emergent giants; typical trees are 10-30 m
height_m.source: WP: 'an up to 60 m tall tree with large plank buttresses' (Gribel et al. 1999). UTP gives 'capable of reaching a height of 70 metres, though it is more likely to be within the range 10 - 30 metres' (Jensen 1999, FAO; World Agroforestry Centre).

crown_width_m.source: WP: 'a crown of foliage as much as 60 m (200 ft) in width' (Carder 2005, p. 129).

trunk_diameter_m.source: UTP: 'The straight, cylindrical bole can be 100 - 300cm in diameter' (Jensen 1999, FAO).

branching.source: WP: 'These major branches, usually 4 to 6 in number, can be up to 1.8 m thick' (Gamlin & de Rohan 1998).

leaf_type.source: WP: 'The palmately divided leaves are composed of 5-9 (-15) leaflets' (PROTA4U).

leaf_length_m.source: WP: 'the leaflets 5-21 cm long' (PROTA4U). Leaflet length, not whole-leaf span.

persistence.source: UTP: 'Ceiba pentandra is a deciduous tree' (Jensen 1999).

not_modelled: plank buttresses (WP: extend 12-15 m up the trunk)

branching.source: WP: 'a large, emergent crown of long branches above the surrounding canopy' (uncited sentence, low confidence).

clear_bole_fraction.source: UTP: the bole 'is unbranched until near the top' (Huxley 1992; Dodge 1897).

branching.source: UTP: 'a few stout branches arising high on the trunk and curving upward' (Little & Wadsworth 1964).
